findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There were various Time/Temperature control (TCS) foods stored inside of the prep cooler that were probed between 45F - 50F. These items included salads, mayonnaise, cheeses, meats, and dressings. The PIC mentioned that the cooler had recently been restocked at 1:30pm after lunch. The facility was instructed to place bulk items back into the walk in cooler and to use time control for the items at the top of the cooler. The facility will discard items after four hours. Ensure that TCS foods are held at 41F or below. Will follow up on July 6, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The prep cooler had an ambient temperature of 50F. See violation #22 for further details. Ensure that the prep cooler is sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. Will follow up on July 6, 2026 to see that the cooler has been serviced or replaced.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The service prep cooler did not contain an internal thermometer to measure the ambient temperature. Discussed with the PIC. Ensure that an internal thermometer is available to accurately measure ambient temperatures of cold holding equipment. Will follow-up on July 6, 2026 to see that the unit has a thermometer available.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: There isn’t any hot water available at the kitchen’s handsink. Employees mentioned that there was hot water available earlier in the day. The water was left running for a few minutes and never came available. Hot water was available at every other sink in the facility, however, hot water shall be available at each handsink to ensure that hands are getting washed properly. Will follow-up on 2/6/2026.
findings.citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The cove base underneath the triple sink is pulling away from the wall. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that cove base is secured to the wall to avoid accumulated debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
A build-up of ice was observed on the ceiling and floor (underneath shelves) of the walk-in freezer. Discussed with PIC to maintain the build up of ice inside of the walk-in freezer. Ensure that equipment and floors are cleaned as necessary to prevent ice build-up.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
